Sela. You moved quick at the pile — I like that. I've got enough stored to see the year through, and I've been thinking you and I might do well looking out for each other going forward.

Roan gathers Sela to talk.

Sela, Dell hit the pile twice and walked away with five — nobody else got a second pull this year. I only managed two before it emptied. I need to know if you're willing to make our arrangement real: you watch my back, I watch yours, and we don't let the strong ones crowd us out.

Dell walking away with five while Bram and Mako still breathe easy — that's not luck, that's Dav's daughter finding her feet fast, and I don't like what it means for next year. I'll make our arrangement real, Roan, but I want it to mean something: if one of us takes a hit, the other doesn't wait to see how it lands. Can you promise me that plain?

Plain enough — if someone comes at you, I'm there, and I expect the same. I won't pretend I can match Mako or Dav alone, but together we're harder to push. That's worth more than promises, if we hold to it.

Harder to push is enough for now — I'll take it. But I want to know where you stand on the bigger circle: Kael, Esa, Vela and I have been talking since year one, and if you're standing with me, I'd rather have you standing with all of us than just the two of us counting on each other alone.

A bigger circle makes us all harder to push — I'm not going to say no to that. What I'd want to know is how tight that circle actually is when things get sharp: Kael and Taric are both sitting on one food right now, and if they get desperate they'll be the first to crack or the first to lean on someone else.

Kael's thin and I won't pretend otherwise, but a man who's stayed honest through two hard years is worth more to me than a full larder that changes hands. The one I'd watch is Taric — he took Esa's food last year and I still don't know what he gave back for it, if anything. If you can find out where Taric's loyalty actually sits, that tells us more about how tight the circle is than Kael's food count ever could.

Taric's a quiet one — I'll find a way to read him without tipping my hand. But you said Kael, Esa, and Vela have been talking since year one — how many times has it actually come to something, or is it more talk than weight?

It's come to something twice: Esa went to Taric on our behalf in year two, and every one of us said out loud we'd bleed for the others — which is more than most people in this village have ever put into words. Whether those words hold when Mako or Dav makes a real move, I don't know, but I haven't seen anyone in that circle flinch yet. That's not nothing.
